title: The Impact of Digital Content Marketing on Brand Equity and Purchase Intention: A Study of Green Food Packaging in Thailand
affiliations: and Faculty of Administration and Information Technology, Rajamangala University of Technology Suvarnabhumi, Thailand

detail.title: The Impact of Digital Content Marketing on Brand Equity and Purchase Intention: A Study of Green Food Packaging in Thailand
detail.abstract: The shifting consumer preference towards eco-friendly packaging and rising awareness regarding the negative effects of traditional packaging on the environment is augmenting the demand for the green packaging. This research aims to reveal the effect of green packaging of food products, which is communicated through digital content marketing activities on social media, which further affects the brand and purchase intention. The research emphasizes the concepts of digital content marketing, customer-based brand equity, and purchase intention. This study assessed the effect of digital content marketing (DCM) of food products with green packaging on customer-based brand equity's dimensions, including brand awareness (BA), brand image (BI), and brand loyalty (BL); and then the effect of DCM on the purchase intention (PI) among Gen Y consumers in Thailand. The study also assessed the interrelation among the customer-based brand equity's dimensions (BA, BI, and BL) and their effects on the purchase intention (PI). This quantitative research gathered data from 500 respondents who were Gen Y consumers (23-43 years old) in Thailand through an online questionnaire survey on Google Forms. Statistical software was applied for conducting the Structural Equations Modelling (SEM). SEM analysis is based on a two-step approach comprising of Measurement Model Assessment and Structural Model Assessment. The results revealed the effect of DCM on BA which was positive and significant in this study. The results revealed that there was no effect of DCM on BI and BL in this study. The results also revealed that the effect of DCM on PI was positive but insignificant in this study. The results revealed that only the effect of BI on BL was significant in this study, with a positive effect. In addition, the results revealed that the effect of BI on PI was positive and significant in this study. It is recommended that the quality of content plays a significant role in creating a brand image, which in turn will have more positive effect on consumer buying intention. Creative content about the brand's CSR activities and environmental campaigns should be used on social media.

title: One Consumer, Multiple Locations: Geographic Targeting with Registration Data under Privacy Constraints
affiliations: London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Department of Management

detail.title: One Consumer, Multiple Locations: Geographic Targeting with Registration Data under Privacy Constraints
detail.abstract: When a platform observes several plausible locations for the same consumer, more location data are not automatically better. The central targeting question is which location signal earns its privacy cost. Using 110,326 transactions from a Chinese live-event ticketing platform, including 63,559 verified orders linking national-ID origin, mobile-number locality, and event location, we study geographic targeting with multiple registration-based locations. Three findings emerge. First, mobile locality is closer to realized consumption than national-ID origin in 58.5% of validated transactions, even though 45.0% of mobile-event distances exceed 500 kilometers. Second, origin-mobile divergence predicts purchases outside both registered locations but not broader distance demand; once purchase-history trajectories are available, they dominate registration signals (.898 AUC). Third, adding national-ID origin to a mobile-only ranker changes AUC by .004 in cold-start, .024 in mid-history, and -.019 in rich-history; none passes the score-increment permutation test. The managerial implication is a sequencing rule for privacy-constrained targeting: start with mobile-location features, keep spatial and taste ranking separate, and process sensitive origin data only when segment-level lift is large enough to justify consent.

detail.abstract:
Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems play an important role in helping organizations improve the way they interact and communicate with customers. This study discusses how CRM systems are used to organize customer information, manage transactions, and provide faster and more efficient services. It highlights the importance of maintaining strong customer relationships to increase satisfaction, loyalty, and overall business performance. The paper also explains how technology helps organizations better understand customer needs and improve decision-making processes.

Furthermore, the study explores the benefits and challenges of implementing CRM systems in organizations. Among the benefits identified are improved productivity, better customer service, and more organized business operations. However, challenges such as system costs, employee adjustment, and data management were also considered. Overall, the study concludes that CRM systems are valuable tools that help organizations become more customer-focused and competitive in today’s modern business environment.

title: Effects of Depression, Anxiety & Stress on Academic Achievement of Bangladeshi Students
affiliations: University of East Anglia (UEA) - School of International Development and

detail.title: Effects of Depression, Anxiety & Stress on Academic Achievement of Bangladeshi Students

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest among the authors, or with any other authority.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based on a review of existing literature and secondary sources. No primary data involving human participants were collected. Therefore, ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This paper received no funding.
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: This study did not involve any clinical trials.

detail.abstract:
Achievement in academics in Bangladesh is closely associated with the future career opportunities, social mobility and family expectations and thus students are highly susceptible to mental turmoil. With the education system mainly being based on high-stakes tests, the struggle to secure a scarce number of university spots, mental problems like depression, anxiety, and stress have emerged as a common occurrence. This dissertation explores the connection between depression, anxiety, stress, and academic achievement of the students based on the psychological theories developed and exhaustive review of international and Bangladeshi empirical researches. 
The research comes up with a conceptual model that incorporates theories of cognitive, stressbased, motivational, and resource-oriented theories to demonstrate how psychological distress is connected with academic performance via cognitive, emotional, and behavioral mechanisms. According to evidence provided by the reviewed literature, depression, anxiety, and stress were always linked to poor academic performance, poor concentration, low motivation, burnout, and high risk of academic disengagement and dropout. The situation in Bangladesh shows more pressure due to parental expectations, economic condition, competition in the admissions tests and inaccessibility to the services of mental health care. 
The review also confirms the existence of reverse causality whereby the poor academic performance worsens the psychological distress which forms a self-reinforcement loop between academic performance and psychological distress. The results in general indicate that mental health cannot exist separately of academic achievement. The dissertation highlights how academic and mental health interventions should be integrated in the Bangladeshi educational institutions so that the students' well-being and future academic prosperity can be fostered.

title: AI Tokenomics and the Firm

detail.title: AI Tokenomics and the Firm
detail.abstract: Generative AI is often described as a general-purpose technology that lowers the cost of prediction, language, and code generation. Yet organizations do not adopt AI in the abstract. They produce output through bundles of tasks, and AI changes production only when a task can be decomposed, matched to a model capability, supplied with relevant context, validated, and reintegrated into a workflow. This paper develops a task-based theory of AI adoption in which the key organizational input is process capital: the managerial capacity to redesign workflows, allocate decision rights, govern data access, monitor quality, and route work between humans and AI systems. Tokens enter the theory not as the primitive economic object, but as the metering and pricing layer for AI-mediated task execution. Token prices affect the cost of AI services, but realized productivity depends on whether firms can convert raw model use into effective task output. The framework distinguishes AI exposure from AI deployability and shows why two firms facing the same model prices may obtain very different returns from AI. Better-managed firms should generate more quality-adjusted output per AI dollar because process capital raises the productivity of AI services and reduces token waste through prompting discipline, caching, routing, and validation. A calibrated simulation using occupational AI exposure scores, employment weights, and wages illustrates the mechanism: under baseline parameters, moving from low to high process capital raises median simulated AI-labor intensity from 0.149 to 0.420 while reducing mean tokens per unit of output from 25.7 to 15.3. The paper connects the economics of AI to task production, management, data as an asset, and law-and-economics theories of measurement and contracting.

title: The Agentic GTM Stack A Comprehensive Conceptual Framework for Autonomous Market Validation, Enterprise Cognition, and Human-Guided Go-To-Market Systems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Agentic GTM Stack A Comprehensive Conceptual Framework for Autonomous Market Validation, Enterprise Cognition, and Human-Guided Go-To-Market Systems
detail.abstract: Traditional go-to-market systems were historically constrained by manual workflows, fragmented tooling, and operational bottlenecks. Recent advances in large language models, orchestration systems, and persistent memory infrastructure have enabled the rise of agentic GTM systems. This paper introduces "The Agentic GTM Stack," a conceptual framework describing how autonomous yet human-guided AI systems transform outbound from a transactional sales mechanism into a persistent market cognition architecture. The framework proposes seven interconnected layers: Infrastructure, Market Intelligence, Identity, Orchestration, Cognitive, Execution, and Memory. Together, these layers enable startups and enterprises to rapidly validate product-market fit, compress learning cycles, accelerate trust formation, and continuously adapt based on real-world market interaction.

title:
The Accountability Gap
Why AI Can Do the Work But Cannot Hold the Role

detail.title:
The Accountability Gap
Why AI Can Do the Work But Cannot Hold the Role

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This paper is a theory-building contribution. Its constructs are proposed on theoretical grounds and supported by their explanatory power over empirical anomalies that existing frameworks predict incorrectly. They have not been subjected to systematic empirical testing. The paper specifies five explicit falsification conditions and a research programme through which empirical validation can proceed. Readers should interpret its propositions as theoretically grounded research directions, not validated findings. The research programme is what this paper proposes. The framework is the invitation.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The author declares no conflicts of interest. No external funding was received for this research. This paper was produced independently through the EXEGESIS research programme.
declarations.funderStatement: The author declares no conflicts of interest. No external funding was received for this research. This paper was produced independently through the EXEGESIS research programme.

detail.abstract: Something is not adding up. Current AI systems can technically perform tasks equivalent to approximately 11.7% of US workforce wage value — roughly $1.2 trillion — according to the MIT–Oak Ridge Iceberg Index, the most computationally rigorous skills-exposure measurement available. Eloundou and colleagues (2024), in Science, find that 80% of the US workforce has at least 10% of their tasks amenable to large language model performance. Yet the Anthropic Economic Index, drawing on observed usage patterns from millions of Claude interactions, finds that 57% of actual AI deployment is augmentative rather than substitutive — humans enhanced, not replaced. Role elimination, while real in concentrated domains, remains modest relative to the capability estimates. Legal employment has held despite AI systems that outperform junior lawyers on document drafting, precedent research, and contract synthesis. Radiologist positions have persisted despite AI diagnostic imaging tools achieving superhuman accuracy on benchmark classification tasks. Social workers remain legally required participants in child protection decisions that AI systems could process in seconds. The frameworks that generated this capability estimates were not wrong. The predictions they imply — that high technical exposure produces proportional human displacement — are not supported by what is actually happening. The gap has a name. We call it the accountability gap: the structural distance between what AI systems can technically perform and what institutional systems require humans to hold. The accountability gap exists because roles are not constituted only by their task content. They are constituted by the legitimacy functions their participation anchors — the accountability relationships, the trust dependencies, the symbolic authority structures, and the institutional validation requirements that determine whether outputs are valid, binding, and attributable to a human who can be held responsible. Every major existing framework measures the first dimension. None models the second. The result is a systematic and directionally predictable misclassification of which roles AI will eliminate and which it will transform. This paper introduces the Functional Cognitive Economics Taxonomy (FCET) to close this gap. FCET formally separates functional automability (FA) — the degree to which a role's task content can be performed by AI at equivalent quality and cost — from institutional replaceability (IR) — the degree to which the coordination function a role serves can be removed from human participation without destabilising the institutional system's trust, accountability, legitimacy, and adaptive coherence. bot is less capable, but because it mediates the procedural experience through which surgical judgment develops.

title: Mandatory Deadlines and Human Capital Accumulation: Evidence from a Natural Experiment in Higher Education
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Mandatory Deadlines and Human Capital Accumulation: Evidence from a Natural Experiment in Higher Education
detail.abstract: In flexible academic environments, students often face weak incentives for sustained effort, which can facilitate procrastination and delay the accumulation of human capital. This study exploits a natural experiment at a German university where two programs introduced course-completion deadlines in 2016-one early and targeted (first-semester), the other delayed and comprehensive (second-year). Using administrative panel data covering over 11,500 students and difference-indifferences (DiD) estimation, I find that early deadlines increased first-year credits by 18% and graduation rates by 7 percentage points. The delayed deadline generated similar effect magnitudes-with effects reaching statistical significance only in propensity-score matched and synthetic DiD specifications. Dropout rates and GPA remained unchanged in both regimes, indicating improvements stem from increased effort rather than selection. Broadly distributed effects across ability levels suggest these deadlines serve as universal pacing tools, enabling institutions to generate academic momentum and improve human capital accumulation without sacrificing equity.

title: BRANDING AS A STRATEGIC TOOL FOR THE SURVIVAL AND GROWTH OF BUSINESSES IN COMPETITIVE MARKETS: A STUDY OF INDIAN SMES
affiliations: Delhi University Enclave

detail.title: BRANDING AS A STRATEGIC TOOL FOR THE SURVIVAL AND GROWTH OF BUSINESSES IN COMPETITIVE MARKETS: A STUDY OF INDIAN SMES
detail.abstract: In today's highly competitive business environment, branding has emerged as a crucial strategic tool for the survival and growth of businesses, particularly for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). Indian SMEs operate in markets characterized by intense competition, price sensitivity, and limited resources, making long-term sustainability a major challenge. This study aims to examine the role of branding as a strategic tool in enhancing the survival and growth of Indian SMEs in competitive markets. The research explores key branding dimensions such as brand identity, brand positioning, brand trust, and digital branding, and analyses their impact on business performance indicators including customer retention, market expansion, and sales growth. A descriptive research design is adopted, using primary data collected from selected Indian SMEs through structured questionnaires, supported by secondary data from existing literature, reports, and journals. The data is analysed using appropriate statistical tools to identify the relationship between branding practices and business outcomes. The findings indicate that SMEs with well-defined branding strategies are better positioned to differentiate themselves, build customer trust, and achieve sustainable growth. Digital branding is found to be a cost-effective and influential tool in improving brand visibility and competitiveness. The study concludes that branding is not merely a promotional activity but a long-term strategic investment essential for the survival and growth of Indian SMEs.

title: Detecting AI Coding Tool Adoption and Its Behavioural Effects on Developer Commit Activity

detail.title: Detecting AI Coding Tool Adoption and Its Behavioural Effects on Developer Commit Activity
detail.abstract:
We study the effect of AI coding tool adoption on developer commit behaviour using two complementary empirical designs. First, we build a behavioural classifier that identifies AI coding tool users from observable commit history — without relying on explicit self-reported adoption or proprietary telemetry. The classifier achieves cross-validated AUC of 0.94 on a sample of 276 GitHub accounts (74 confirmed adopters, 202 controls) and generalises to users of a second tool (Aider, mean predicted probability 0.73) it was never trained on, suggesting it detects general AI-assisted coding behaviour rather than tool-specific stylistic artefacts.

Second, we use the classifier in two causal designs. An account-level difference-in-differences finds large, statistically significant changes in commit behaviour for AI adopters relative to controls, including substantial increases in commits per active week and reductions in inter-commit hours. A country-level panel regression across 34 countries (2022–2024) finds divergent results across dependent variables: a robust negative association between adoption and commits per developer (weighted coefficient = −7.56, p = 0.05 across 34 countries) coexists with a precisely-estimated null on pull requests per developer (coefficient = +1.33, p = 0.76). We interpret this DV split cautiously: it is consistent with AI tools shifting commit granularity (fewer, larger commits) rather than reducing genuine output, but our data cannot rule out alternative explanations.

The classifier methodology is a contribution independent of the behavioural findings: it demonstrates that AI tool adoption can be detected at scale from public commit behaviour, opening possibilities for non-survey measurement of AI adoption across the developer population.

title: Generative AI Fuels Solo Entrepreneurship, but Teams Still Lead at the Top
affiliations: Seoul National University, Seoul National University and Seoul National University

detail.title: Generative AI Fuels Solo Entrepreneurship, but Teams Still Lead at the Top
detail.abstract: <u>Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping who enters entrepreneurship, but not who reaches the top of the quality distribution. Using data on over 160,000 product launches on Product Hunt, we find that entrepreneurial entry increased sharply following the public release of ChatGPT-3.5, driven disproportionately by solo entrepreneurs. This shift toward solo entry is particularly pronounced in categories that historically favored team-based ventures. However, much of this growth reflects low-commitment, experimental entry and does not translate into greater representation among the highest-quality outcomes. Team-based ventures are increasingly dominant in the top tiers of platform rankings. These findings suggest that generative AI lowers barriers to solo entrepreneurship while reinforcing team-based advantages.</u>

The term "brand" has undergone definitional collapse, rendering it operationally useless for systematic implementation, academic teaching, and measurable outcomes (Davoudi, 2025a). The Law of Emotional Consistency further establishes that lasting emotional connection requires predictable behavioural patterns over time, not isolated moments of resonance (Davoudi, 2025b). However, the term "brand" cannot be rehabilitated through methodological refinement, because frameworks built on a definitionally collapsed term inherit its definitional incoherence. This paper introduces Genobrand, a new term with operational definition, scientific foundation, and methodology that "brand" has functionally tried to acquire but never operationally achieved. Genobrand is defined as an entity whose engineered integration of articulated purpose, articulated promise, and systematic behavioural proof produces lasting emotional connection with the audience it is engineered to reach. The framework is governed by the Attention Formula: (Purpose + Promise) × Proof = Lasting Emotional Connection, where Purpose and Promise constitute the linguistic articulation layer and Proof constitutes the behavioural demonstration layer. The multiplicative structure indicates that behavioural proof is not additive but multiplicative; in its absence, articulated identity produces no lasting connection regardless of strength. The paper consolidates eight peer-reviewed principles from neuroscience, cognitive psychology, and behavioural economics into a unified operational methodology, situating Genobrand as integration-based applied science in the tradition of Darwin's integration of natural history into evolutionary theory and Einstein's integration of physics into relativity. The paper positions Genobrand against existing brand theory frameworks (Aaker, Keller, Kapferer), the archetypal tradition (Mark and Pearson), adjacent frameworks frequently applied to brand (Sinek, Miller), and the empirical marketing science tradition (Sharp), demonstrating that each operates on the post-collapse meaning of "brand" through application of the substitution test established in Davoudi (2025a). Systematic empirical validation through controlled studies, with appropriate comparison conditions and replication, represents the next research phase. The paper generates falsifiable predictions and establishes a research agenda for component-level validation.

title: Decoding Quality Classifications: The Role of Terroir, Labor and Reputation in German Fine Wine Pricing
affiliations: University of Witten/Herdecke, University of Witten/Herdecke and

detail.title: Decoding Quality Classifications: The Role of Terroir, Labor and Reputation in German Fine Wine Pricing

declarations.funderStatement: Funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation). Project number: 533541634.

detail.abstract: Wine markets exemplify experience goods, with prices shaped less by ex ante spec-ified product characteristics than by non-material attributes coordinated through con-ventions and expert evaluations. We identify the power of collective and individual reputation mechanisms as main quality signals in a German fine wine cohort. The setting is the VDP, a private German association that codifies a terroir-oriented high quality regime. A hedonic price regression is estimated for VDP single-vineyard wines, covering 1646 wines from 185 of the 202 VDP wineries across all German wine regions. The internal classification of the VDP explains a large share of price variation (57.7% of the variation explained by our model), with higher tiers associated with sizeable premia (a 97.5% premium from lowest to highest tier). Individual reputation remains positive and significant but primarily differentiates within classification tiers. The find-ings indicate that the VDP operates as a valuable collective-reputation mechanism that coordinates willingness to pay and exercises interpretive authority over quality-relevant production conditions: origin and vineyard work function as complementary quality markers with measurable price effects.

title: Personalized Depression: Algorithmic Pricing, the Inversion of the Price Signal, and the Atomization of Consumer Markets
affiliations: University of the Cumberlands

detail.title: Personalized Depression: Algorithmic Pricing, the Inversion of the Price Signal, and the Atomization of Consumer Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract: Algorithmic pricing systems, powered by machine learning and enabled by the rapid deployment of electronic shelf labels in brick-and-mortar retail, are transforming how consumer goods are priced. This paper argues that personalized pricing does not merely adjust price magnitudes but transforms the institutional function of the price itself, converting it from a public coordination signal into a private instrument of individualized surplus extraction. Drawing on information economics (Hayek, 1945; Grossman & Stiglitz, 1980), the welfare economics of price discrimination (Bergemann et al., 2015), and the structural analysis of algorithmic inequality (O’Neil, 2016; Benjamin, 2019; Eubanks, 2018), the paper develops the concept of “personalized depression”: a condition in which each consumer is subjected to a bespoke economic squeeze, calibrated by algorithm to their inferred tolerance, invisible to every other consumer, and therefore immune to the comparison and collective response that have historically disciplined pricing power. The paper makes three contributions. First, it introduces the “Hayek inversion thesis,” demonstrating that personalized pricing reverses the direction of informational service in the price system, from serving market participants to serving market operators. Second, it dismantles the efficiency defense of algorithmic pricing on its own terms, engaging directly with Dubé and Misra (2023), Castillo (2025), and Rhodes and Zhou (2024) to show that the conditions under which personalized pricing improves welfare (supply elasticity, full market coverage, competitive discipline) fail systematically in the essential-goods markets where the technology is being deployed. Third, it establishes personalized pricing as a mechanism of economic stratification, showing that because demand inelasticity for essential goods correlates with income constraint, geographic isolation, and racial segregation, the algorithmic pricing rule can function as a stratification rule that concentrates extraction on the most vulnerable populations. Five theoretical propositions are advanced and linked to operationalizable empirical research designs. The paper treats the accelerating regulatory response across U.S. federal and state jurisdictions as evidence of institutional recognition that the market concerns theorized here have achieved policy salience, and proposes structural transparency (mandatory algorithmic audits combined with protected-class restrictions on pricing inputs) as the regulatory architecture most consistent with its analysis.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Analytics in Modern Business Decision-Making

detail.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Analytics in Modern Business Decision-Making

declarations.declarationOfInterest: “None.”
declarations.ethicsApproval: “Not applicable.”
declarations.funderStatement: “No funding was received for this research.”

detail.abstract: In recent years, digital transformation has significantly reshaped traditional decision-making processes within organizations. The emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Big Data Analytics has enabled organizations to process and analyze large volumes of financial, behavioral, and operational data with unprecedented speed and accuracy. These technologies support managers in making faster, more reliable, and evidence-based decisions in highly competitive business environments. Despite these advantages, the implementation of AI-and data-driven systems is associated with several challenges, including technical complexity, lack of skilled professionals, ethical concerns, data privacy issues, and organizational resistance to technological change. This study examines the role of Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Analytics in improving modern business decision-making and identifies the key requirements for successful implementation. A systematic literature review was conducted based on academic sources published between 2020 and 2025. The findings propose a conceptual framework for improving decision quality, operational efficiency, and organizational competitiveness.

detail.abstract: This paper estimates the causal effect of SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) participation on household per-capita calorie intake using the USDA FoodAPS Public Use File. The analytic sample comprises 4,303 households-1,342 SNAP recipients and 2,961 non-recipients. Five estimators are compared: OLS, nearest-neighbor matching (NN), propensity score matching (PSM), inverse probability weighting (IPW), and doubly-robust IPW regression adjustment (IPWRA). The preferred doubly-robust IPWRA estimate-which is consistent if either the propensity score model or the outcome regression is correctly specified-yields an average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) of-3.82 kcal per capita (p = 0.016, 95% CI: [-6.94,-0.70]). This estimate is modest in magnitude (≈5% of the counterfactual mean) and suggests that SNAP maintains rather than substantially increases per-capita calorie adequacy among participating households. Sign divergence between IPW and IPWRA reveals model dependence, motivating the doubly-robust approach. These findings have direct relevance to current U.S. policy debates surrounding SNAP reform, program evaluation methodology, and the design of nutrition assistance interventions.

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes Haa Latseení — Our Strength: Strength of Body, Mind, and Spirit — as the name for a unified relational transmission theory of intergenerational health. The theory's central claim is that the Dunbar nested layer architecture, operating through Barrett's Theory of Constructed Emotion, with LeDoux's dual-pathway survival circuit model providing the temporal structure, constitutes the intergenerational transmission mechanism for emotional granularity and predictive success — and that its systematic disruption through colonization, structural violence, and nutritional depletion is the primary mechanism through which historical trauma produces multigenerational health effects.

The methodology is translational — moving between Indigenous epistemological frameworks and Western scientific literature to specify the unified architecture that makes both legible simultaneously, grounded in four decades of observational practice and implementation leadership in Alaska Native health and tribal governance.

Five original contributions are advanced: the Gap Layering Model; a two-dimensional PCE typology distinguishing community from dyadic PCEs; circular time as neurobiological mechanism rather than cultural metaphor; campcraft with the Three Feathers protocol as ignition sequence, with relational safety as non-negotiable precondition; and gap width variability as the primary diagnostic indicator of relational architecture integrity following Deming's process control logic. Nutritional restoration provides the metabolic substrate Dunbar layer construction requires.

Eight falsifiable propositions constitute a complete empirical research agenda. The campfire predates medicine by ten thousand years. Haa Latseení explains why.

title: CoDiS: Convex Dictionary-Based Sparse Topic Decomposition for Interpretable Dense Retrieval
affiliations: Hefei Normal University, Anhui University, Anhui University, University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), Hefei Comprehensive National Science Center and University of Science and Technology of China (USTC)

detail.title: CoDiS: Convex Dictionary-Based Sparse Topic Decomposition for Interpretable Dense Retrieval
detail.abstract: Learning dense representations that are simultaneously effective, robust, and interpretable remains a central challenge in dense retrieval. Standard bi-encoder retrievers map each document into a single monolithic vector, which is computationally attractive but tends to entangle multiple latent semantic factors inside one embedding. This entanglement weakens interpretability, reduces controllability of candidate generation, and makes the ranking process vulnerable to hard negatives that are semantically similar to the query yet mismatched in topical intent. We propose CoDiS, a convex dictionary-based sparse topic decomposition architecture for dense retrieval. CoDiS inserts a learnable intermediate topic layer between corpus encoding and document-level matching, where dictionary atoms are obtained through a sparse autoencoder with convex constraints and are therefore grounded in sparse combinations of observed document embeddings rather than unconstrained latent prototypes. This design turns the intermediate representation into a corpus-grounded sparse semantic basis that can be inspected, analyzed, and used for topic-aware candidate filtering. The topic layer is trained jointly with contrastive dense retrieval objectives so that sparse reconstruction and downstream relevance discrimination reinforce one another. Experiments on the BEIR benchmark show that CoDiS achieves strong overall effectiveness and produces especially large gains on datasets characterized by topic diversity, semantic ambiguity, and hard-negative interference. Additional qualitative analyses indicate that the learned sparse activations improve topic coherence and expose meaningful intermediate semantic structure. These results suggest that convex sparse topic decomposition is a useful inductive bias for interpretable and robust neural dense retrieval.

title: Low-Quality Blind Images Enhancement via  Diffusion-Fourier Prior Fusion for Visual Classification
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Low-Quality Blind Images Enhancement via  Diffusion-Fourier Prior Fusion for Visual Classification
detail.abstract: Classic image classification models exhibit limited feature extraction capabilities on low-quality images, struggling to extract discriminative features. This results in suboptimal performance of low-quality images in visual classification tasks. To address the decline in classification accuracy for low-quality images in classic models, this paper proposes a Low-Quality Blind Image Enhancement via Diffusion-Fourier Prior Fusion (LQBIE-DFPF) method that consists of three main components. First, to overcome the limitations of traditional diffusion models, which generate images with coarse details and are prone to blurring and distortion, an Improved Pre-trained Diffusion Model (IPDM) is proposed. Then, a Diffusion-Fourier Prior Fusion (DFPF) module is constructed to generate high-quality images that maintain both statistical properties and semantic feature consistency. Finally, to address the slow generation speed caused by the lengthy iteration steps of diffusion models, a NIQE-based Adaptive Diffusion-step Strategy (NIQE-ADS) is proposed to adapt the diffusion steps and improve computational efficiency. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in enhancing various types of low-quality and degraded images on the ImageNet-C dataset, thereby improving the classification accuracy of such images.

title: Superposition and Polysemanticity in Mamba’s Selective State Space: A Mechanistic Interpretability Study via Sparse Autoencoders
affiliations: , Rajarshi School of Management & Technology, Indian Institute of Technology, Patna and

detail.title: Superposition and Polysemanticity in Mamba’s Selective State Space: A Mechanistic Interpretability Study via Sparse Autoencoders
detail.abstract: State space models (SSMs), particularly the Mamba architecture, have emerged as competitive alternatives to Transformers for sequence modeling, offering linear-time complexity during both training and inference. Despite their growing adoption, the internal representations of SSMs remain poorly understood from an interpretability standpoint. This paper presents the first systematic mechanistic interpretability study of superposition and polysemanticity in Mamba’s selective state space, addressing whether SSM hidden-state channels exhibit representational phenomena analogous to those documented in Transformers. We train 114 TopK sparse autoencoders (SAEs) in a primary experimental campaign across two Mamba models (130M and 370M parameters), two GPT-2 baselines (124M and 355M parameters), multiple network depths, three expansion factors, and three random seeds, using both WikiText-103 (out-of-distribution) and The Pile (in-distribution) corpora. An additional 13 validation SAEs bring the total to 127 trained models. In our experiments we discovered three primary findings. First, Mamba and Transformers use fundamentally different geometric representations of what the activation of each unit represents. In this regard, Mamba's activation is distributed over an approximately five to 179 times larger dimensional manifold than GPT-2's (based upon participation ratio, which is 5.9–179 for Mamba, 1.1–13.4 for GPT-2) with a significantly higher SAE reconstruction error (FVU is 0.181 for Mamba, 0.064 for GPT-2) and consistently less polysemous representation for the same expansion factors (mean Polysemanticity Index 0.473 for Mamba, 0.505 for GPT-2, Cohen's d = 0.54) and therefore, the SSM's state accumulation process disperses representations throughout a number of hidden dimensions as opposed to condensing these into a relatively small subspace through superposition. Second, the selective differential sparsification analysis demonstrated that the delta gate projection (dt_proj) is a significant selectivity bottleneck; when only 10% of the elements in dt_proj were pruned, there was a complete collapse of perplexity (+290 PPL), whereas pruning at the same rate the x_proj and in_proj elements had little impact on perplexity (ΔPPL < 1), a sensitivity differential that does not exist within the Transformer attention projections. Finally, by employing an activation patching approach, we demonstrated that there are substantial differences in causal structure between Mamba and GPT-2. Specifically, patching Mamba's mixer output resulted in near zero restoration (range -0.122 to +0.018), while the same type of patching applied to GPT-2's residual streams resulted in perfect restoration (1.0 at every layer) and demonstrated that the recurrent states in Mamba carry information that is independent of the residual stream. The findings presented above have been validated through cross-dataset consistency (PI r = 0.934, p = 0.006; SI r = 0.988, p < 0.001), sequence length robustness (seq128 vs. seq512 ΔPI < 0.01), and TopK sensitivity analysis (k = 16/32/64).

title: A Novel Active Sample Acquisition Strategy with Sinkhorn Distance-based Sensitivity
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Novel Active Sample Acquisition Strategy with Sinkhorn Distance-based Sensitivity
detail.abstract: While deep learning has demonstrated remarkable success across various domains, its performance critically depends on the availability of large-scale labeled data, which is often expensive and labour-intensive to obtain. Active learning offers a cost-effective alternative by selecting the most informative samples from an unlabeled pool for annotation. Existing methods identify such samples by estimating predictive uncertainty. They rely on complex training schemes such as adversarial learning or auxiliary models, resulting in intricate and inefficient pipelines that are difficult to scale in practice. These techniques ignore the distributional structure of the data and tend to become unreliable in low-label regimes due to model overconfidence. In this work, we propose a novel acquisition strategy based on optimal transport theory, which quantifies how much an unlabeled sample perturbs the alignment between the labeled and unlabeled data distributions. By leveraging a smooth and computationally efficient Sinkhorn distance, we compute the sensitivity of the distributional transport cost to a sample. This enables us to move beyond point-wise uncertainty and capture informativeness at a structural level. The proposed method utilizes both the labeled and unlabeled data in the acquisition process, making it more efficient and effective in case of fewer labels. The proposed approach is model-agnostic, easy to implement, and free of data-dependent tricks. It consistently outperforms baselines on benchmarks such as CIFAR10, SVHN, CIFAR-100 and CalTech-101 for image classification tasks. In particular, it demonstrates a superior performance in low-budget regimes, where the distributional structure is critical.

title: Structured Multidimensional Representation Learning for Large Language Models
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Mohammed VI Polytechnic University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Structured Multidimensional Representation Learning for Large Language Models
detail.abstract: Transformer architectures achieve state-of-the-art performance across a wide range of pattern recognition and natural language processing tasks, but their scaling is accompanied by substantial parameter growth and redundancy in the embedding dimension. In this work, we introduce a structured spectral factorization of the embedding space based on the L-product for third-order tensors. By reshaping token representations into spectral tensor slices and performing attention and feed-forward operations in the transform domain, we obtain a Tensor Transformer architecture that decomposes the encoder into p independent spectral sub-transformers while preserving standard Transformer semantics. We prove that the proposed L-Transformer is spectrally equivalent to p parallel Transformers operating on reduced-dimensional embeddings, which yields approximately 1/p reduction (up to lower-order terms such as biases and normalization parameters) in encoder parameters under fixed total embedding size. When instantiated with a real-valued Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), the method remains fully differentiable and compatible with existing training pipelines. Beyond compression, the spectral decomposition introduces an inductive bias over embedding frequencies, enabling slice-dependent frequency scaling that improves generalization. Experiments on IMDB and AG~News show that the proposed model can substantially reduce encoder parameters (up to 75\% for p=4) while maintaining competitive accuracy. On IMDB, the tensorized encoder matches or improves upon the standard baseline under compression, whereas on AG~News at moderate width we observe a small accuracy decrease in exchange for a 4 times encoder reduction; at BERT-base width (d=768), performance returns to parity.

title: PRISM: Distilling Multi-Source Priors for Single-Image Avatar Reconstruction
affiliations: Hangzhou Dianzi University, Hangzhou Dianzi University, The University of Sydney, Hangzhou Dianzi University and The University of Sydney

detail.title: PRISM: Distilling Multi-Source Priors for Single-Image Avatar Reconstruction
detail.abstract: Creating animatable 3D human avatars from a single image is a highly ill-posed problem that demands strong priors to resolve the inherent depth, appearance, and articulation ambiguities. Existing methods typically rely on a single category of prior, either learned parametric models or data-driven generative networks, and consequently struggle to recover faithful geometry, photorealistic appearance, and plausible dynamics simultaneously, especially for unseen regions. We present \textbf{PRISM}, an approach that synergistically distills \emph{multi-source} knowledge, including multi-view diffusion priors, video diffusion priors, and parametric body priors, into a unified SMPL-X-anchored 2D Gaussian Splatting representation. PRISM adopts a dual-branch architecture: a \emph{Static Branch} that leverages multi-view diffusion models to hallucinate consistent novel views for full-body appearance and geometry reconstruction, and a \emph{Dynamic Branch} that exploits video diffusion models to learn plausible motion-dependent deformations. To harmonize these heterogeneous supervision signals, we introduce \emph{Knowledge-Aware Synergistic Training (KAST)}, a three-layer coordination mechanism comprising gradient routing, confidence-weighted loss aggregation, and progressive knowledge injection that resolves inter-source conflicts while maximizing complementary benefits. Extensive experiments on the NeuMan and X-Humans benchmarks demonstrate that PRISM consistently outperforms existing methods across rendering quality and geometric accuracy metrics, establishing new state-of-the-art results for single-image animatable avatar generation. Code will be released upon acceptance at \href{https://github.com/loong8888/PRISM}{here}.

title: Borders, Conflict Legacies, and Fire: Introducing Socio-Political Landscape Factors for Wildfire Risk in Geopolitically Fragile Regions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Borders, Conflict Legacies, and Fire: Introducing Socio-Political Landscape Factors for Wildfire Risk in Geopolitically Fragile Regions
detail.abstract: This study uses a geospatial framework to introduces Socio-Political Landscape Factors (SPLFs), spatial variables representing governance discontinuities, conflict legacies, and restricted-access conditions, as predictors of wildfire incidence across the Kurdish borderlands, focusing on the Kurdistan Region (KR) of northern Iraq and Kurdish-dominant regions of western Iran. Using Sentinel-2 burned-area data (2019–2025), georeferenced landmine maps, and administrative boundaries, we define two domains: a broad geopolitical domain (Scenario 1) and a restricted border-adjacent domain (Scenario 2). Spatial-overlap analysis and a distance-weighted sampling framework (~20,000 points) were used to train Logistic Regression (LR) and Random Forest (RF) models. Results show pronounced proximity effects: in Scenario 1, 36.3% of burned areas are within 0–5 km of borders and 54.1% of minefields, rising to 41.3% and 60.3% in Scenario 2. Distance bands of 0–10 km account for most fires. Logistic models reveal significant negative distance coefficients (β ≈ −0.04 to −0.06), indicating a 4–6% reduction in wildfire odds per additional kilometer from borders or minefields. RF corroborate elevated fire probabilities near these features (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Curve (AUC) ≈ 0.60–0.74). Findings demonstrate SPLFs improve wildfire risk mapping in politically complex landscapes, though predictive precision is limited by data gaps and missing environmental covariates.

title: Reliable and Global Gaussian Alignment for Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
affiliations: Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, National University of Singapore, Nankai University and Nanjing University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Reliable and Global Gaussian Alignment for Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
detail.abstract: Test-time adaptation (TTA) has attracted increasing attention as an effective paradigm for improving the performance of vision-language models (VLMs) on unseen test data during inference, without requiring annotations. However, existing TTA methods struggle to consistently accumulate reliable information from streaming test data. Cache-based methods suffer from limited cache capacity, leading to catastrophic forgetting of earlier samples, thus preventing global information accumulation. In contrast, statistical updating methods attempt to accumulate information across the entire test stream, but they directly incorporate all predictions without any selection of high-confidence samples, causing error accumulation from unreliable predictions. In this paper, we propose REGAIN, a Reliable and Global Gaussian Alignment test-time adaptation framework designed to address these limitations. REGAIN employs a dynamic entropy queue that selects high-confidence samples and effectively filters out unreliable predictions during inference. Building upon these selected samples, REGAIN incrementally updates class-conditional Gaussian distribution in an online manner, allowing the model to accumulate information over time while avoiding error propagation. By combining Bayesian posterior probabilities derived from these robust statistics with zero-shot priors obtained from VLMs’ predictions, REGAIN significantly improves adaptation to test data. Extensive experiments on 15 datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art methods while maintaining high computational efficiency.

title: Does Fulfillment by Amazon boost the Reputation of Third-Party Sellers?
affiliations: Kentucky State University and Purdue University - Department of Agricultural Economics

detail.title: Does Fulfillment by Amazon boost the Reputation of Third-Party Sellers?

declarations.funderStatement: USDA NIFA

detail.abstract: In 2006, Amazon launched the Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) program, providing support to thirdparty sellers for a fee. While the program has the potential to enhance sellers' reputations, evidence regarding its effectiveness is limited. This study estimates the impact of FBA usage on seller reputation, measured by the average star rating a seller receives. Using 26 weeks of panel data from Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States, three key findings emerge from fixed effects and staggered adoption estimation approaches. First, using FBA significantly boosts a seller's reputation, leading to higher average ratings in the short term than in the long term. This improvement is mainly due to FBA's competitive advantages, such as eligibility for Amazon Prime, standardized fulfillment quality, and excellent customer service. Second, although FBA impacts are positive in every country, we find crosscountry heterogeneity in effect sizes and significance levels, with the largest effects in Canada. Third, we show that large sellers have the best reputation, and all sellers benefit from the FBA program. However, medium-sized sellers benefit the most from the program. This trend can be attributed to how the benefits of the FBA program accrue optimally to sellers based on their operational scale. These results suggest that the FBA program is indeed effective in enhancing seller reputation, with implications for third-party sellers, Amazon, and regulators.

title: Role of Bioameliorant Composition in Enhancing Nutrient Uptake and Yield of Maize-Soybean Intercropping Systems on Suboptimal Land

detail.title: Role of Bioameliorant Composition in Enhancing Nutrient Uptake and Yield of Maize-Soybean Intercropping Systems on Suboptimal Land
detail.abstract: Maize-soybean intercropping combined with bioameliorant application offers a promising strategy to enhance nutrient uptake and crop productivity on suboptimal land while improving land-use efficiency and reducing dependence on imported soybean.This study aimed to evaluate the role of different bioameliorant compositions in enhancing soil nutrient status, nutrient uptake (nitrogen and phosphorus), and yield in a maize-soybean intercropping system on suboptimal land. The experiment was conducted in 2025 in North Lombok, Indonesia, using a Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) with five treatments and three replications. The experimental soil was classified as suboptimal land, characterized by very low total nitrogen (0.01%) and low soil organic matter content (1.21%), confirming poor soil quality. title: EXAMINING THE LONG TERM RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CRUDE OIL AND FOOD COMMODITY PRICES: CO-INTEGRATION AND CAUSALITY

detail.title: EXAMINING THE LONG TERM RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CRUDE OIL AND FOOD COMMODITY PRICES: CO-INTEGRATION AND CAUSALITY
detail.abstract: Recently a new debate has started regarding food and energy issues because food has become an alternative source of energy and energy becoming the main input of agriculture. However, this study attempts to investigate the possible long-term relationship between the prices of crude oil and food commodities represented by maize, wheat, sorghum, soybean, barley, linseed oil, soybean oil, and palm oil. Time series econometric techniques (Unit root tests, Co-integration, and Granger causality) were applied. The study utilizes monthly data over the period of 1980 to 2009. The results of this study reveal that there is a strong evidence of long-term relationship between crude oil and the food commodities prices. A traditional Granger Causality is used to check whether causality exists between two product prices. The outcome suggests that there is unidirectional causality between the prices crude oil and some of the food commodities under examination.

title: Implementation of AAOIFI standards as a legal basis for partnership financing in international projects involving Russia
affiliations: MGIMO

detail.title: Implementation of AAOIFI standards as a legal basis for partnership financing in international projects involving Russia
detail.abstract: The adoption of the Law on Partnership Financing in the Russian Federation has opened up opportunities for attracting investment from countries where Islamic finance is particularly important, as well as for participating in joint projects with them. Accordingly, the issue of a harmonized legal framework is of para-mount importance, and attention should be given to the implementation of AAOIFI standards now. Of course, the implementation of Sharia laws and prin-ciples in the legal system of a secular state is fraught with conflicts, which will require amendments to civil and tax legislation, as well as the development of a unified approach to the translation and interpretation of key Islamic finance terms.

title: AI and the Dynamics of Conflict: Theory and Experimental Evidence
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), Korea Information Society Development Institute (KISDI), College of Business, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) and University of Stavanger

detail.title: AI and the Dynamics of Conflict: Theory and Experimental Evidence
detail.abstract: This paper examines how AI-generated recommendations influence the dynamics of conflict, in which rational agents preemptively strike out of fear of being exploited. We extend the conflict game of Baliga and Sjöström (2004) by introducing a global-game structure as a modeling device, where the AI recommendation functions as an algorithmic anchor that correlates beliefs across players. Our model predicts that a common algorithmic signal compresses strategic heterogeneity, strengthens belief correlation, and potentially improves joint welfare. We test these predictions in a laboratory experiment in which participants receive recommendations from GPT-5 trained on human behavioral data. The results contradict the optimistic conjecture: AI compresses strategies asymmetrically without shifting the mean, and crowds out rather than strengthens interpersonal co-movement. These forces leave joint welfare unchanged. Our findings suggest that deploying AI at scale demands attention not only to algorithmic accuracy, but to how common algorithmic signals shape collective human behavior.

title: GMDH and NSGA-III based design optimization of bio-inspired cooling systems for prismatic LFP batteries
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: GMDH and NSGA-III based design optimization of bio-inspired cooling systems for prismatic LFP batteries
detail.abstract: This study presents a high-fidelity multi-objective optimization of bio-inspired cold plates (Ginkgo, Tilia, Tulip) for prismatic LFP battery thermal management. The coupled effects of mass flow rate (0.5–20 g/s), inlet temperature (5–30 °C), and glycol volume fraction (0–60%) on maximum battery temperature (Tmax), temperature non-uniformity (ΔT), and pressure drop (ΔP) are systematically examined under a 3C discharge rate. Numerical reliability is confirmed via GCI, with experimental validation showing a 9.83% maximum error. To overcome the limitations of conventional regression, the Group Method of Data Handling (GMDH) is utilized to develop precise surrogate models, which are subsequently coupled with the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) for multi-objective optimization. The optimization identifies a robust feasible Pareto front strictly adhering to the safety constraints of 15°C≤Tmax≤35°C and ΔT≤5°C. Quantitative results reveal ten candidate optimal designs, where Design 1 offers the highest efficiency with a minimum pressure drop of 1058.96 Pa, while Design 10 provides maximum thermal safety with a Tmax of 32.18°C. Furthermore, the integration of freezing-point constraints enables climate-adaptive selection; designs with glycol fractions up to 58.43% ensure system integrity in extreme conditions down to -49°C, albeit with a 58% increase in hydraulic penalty compared to the base optimal design.

title: Human Capital in an AI World
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: Human Capital in an AI World
detail.abstract: We study optimal human capital investment in a model where humans and AI are symmetric learners, identical except in compute and data. AI has a structural limit: its training data contains no first-personal experience-a dimension many AI exposure measures miss as they focus on cognitive complexity. Tasks combine distributional and first-personal skills, and are assigned to either humans or AI. We show that tasks with sufficient first-personal content remain permanently in the human domain, regardless of how cheap AI becomes. As AI cheapens, a Baumol channel raises the wage of first-personal skill, which overtakes ordinary cognitive skill if human-exclusive tasks are sufficiently first-personal-skill intensive. Optimal investment shifts toward first-personal skill; investment in distributional skill is non-monotone-falling as routine cognitive work moves to AI, then recovering.

detail.abstract:
This working draft presents a practical guide to HMRC's Making 
Tax Digital for Income Tax Self Assessment (MTD-ITSA) regime, 
written for self-employed workers, landlords, and their 
professional advisers.

From April 2026, self-employed workers and landlords with gross 
qualifying income above £50,000 are required to maintain digital 
records and submit quarterly updates to HMRC using approved 
software. Further phases extend this obligation to those above 
£30,000 in April 2027 and above £20,000 in April 2028.

The book covers the distinction between quarterly updates and 
tax returns, scope and threshold calculations, the full MTD 
compliance year including quarterly submissions and year-end 
adjustments, common income and expense recording errors, software 
misclassification risks across QuickBooks, FreeAgent, and Xero, 
legitimate expenses frequently under-claimed, capital allowances 
and year-end adjustments, compliance risk signals, record-keeping 
templates, and a thirty-day action plan for the first quarterly 
deadline.

WORKING DRAFT NOTICE: This manuscript is pending technical 
review by a qualified UK tax adviser. All figures, thresholds, 
and rules should be verified against current HMRC guidance at 
gov.uk before being relied upon.

title: ** Financial Anti-Corruption Governance in the Age of Crypto and SWIFT: Russia, China, Iran, and the Geopolitics of Illicit Finance **

detail.title: ** Financial Anti-Corruption Governance in the Age of Crypto and SWIFT: Russia, China, Iran, and the Geopolitics of Illicit Finance **
detail.abstract: This paper examines how anti-corruption governance is reshaped by the interaction of cryptocurrency, SWIFT-based sanctions compliance, and geopolitical financial control in Russia, China, and Iran. It argues that illicit finance increasingly migrates across payment infrastructures rather than disappearing, making traceability, sanctions screening, and institutional transparency central to anti-corruption policy. Using a comparative policy framework, the study links crypto-related crime, sanctions evasion, and financial integrity tools deployed by the United States, SWIFT, and the United Nations system. The paper shows that crypto can function either as a channel for evasion or as an audit-friendly tool when paired with effective governance, while SWIFTbased screening remains a key mechanism for restricting suspicious flows. The analysis contributes to anti-corruption literature by integrating financial security, sanctions architecture, and digital payment governance into a single framework. It concludes that effective anti-corruption policy requires a combined regime of traceability, compliance, and institutional accountability .

title: A Dynamic Collaborative Sharing Dung Beetle Optimization Algorithm for Coverage and Energy Efficiency in Soil Wireless Sensor Networks
affiliations: Shihezi University, Shihezi University, Shihezi University, Shihezi University and Shihezi University

detail.title: A Dynamic Collaborative Sharing Dung Beetle Optimization Algorithm for Coverage and Energy Efficiency in Soil Wireless Sensor Networks
detail.abstract: In agricultural monitoring, the deployment of soil wireless sensor networks (WSNs) often faces inherent conflicts among coverage rate, network energy consumption, and environmental robustness. To address this multi-objective optimization problem, this paper proposes a Dynamic Collaborative Sharing Dung Beetle Optimization algorithm (DCSDBO) for coverage and energy efficiency optimization in soil WSNs. First, departing from the conventional ideal sensing model, a dynamic sensing model is constructed by coupling key soil parameters including temperature, humidity, electrical conductivity (EC), and NPK content to characterize real-world coverage quality. Second, the DCSDBO algorithm integrates Circle chaotic mapping, cosine adaptive weighting, Sigmoid nonlinear dynamic adjustment, and information collaborative sharing strategies, achieving enhanced global optimization capability and convergence accuracy in complex multi-objective search spaces through the synergistic complementarity of multiple mechanisms. Benchmark tests on CEC2017 and multi-constrained farmland simulations demonstrate that the DCSDBO algorithm effectively mitigates node redundancy and yields superior deployment schemes. Furthermore, field deployment experiments in real farmland environments show that, compared with rule-based empirical deployment strategies, the DCSDBO optimized network achieves a 20.67% improvement in effective coverage rate and a 16.70% reduction in total energy consumption. This work not only achieves an effective balance between node coverage and energy consumption, but also provides an efficient solution for intelligent monitoring in precision agriculture.

title: Deep learning hybrid models with attention mechanisms for ship fuel oil consumption prediction: A comparative study
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Strathclyde and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Deep learning hybrid models with attention mechanisms for ship fuel oil consumption prediction: A comparative study
detail.abstract: Accurate prediction of ship fuel oil consumption (FOC) is essential for operational cost control, emissions reporting, and regulatory compliance. This study evaluates deep learning models for nowcasting instantaneous FOC of a tanker vessel’s diesel generator using high-frequency engine-room data. A dataset comprising 41,760 one-minute measurements of 16 operational parameters was pre-processed using time-series windowing and used to train 17 standalone and hybrid architectures, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and three variants of attention mechanisms: Self-Attention, Multi-Head Attention, and Contextual Attention. Model performance was assessed using cross validated error metrics. The CNN–LSTM–Self Attention architecture achieved the highest accuracy across 6 of 8 metrics, including the lowest mean squared error and mean absolute error, and the highest coefficient of determination. Architectures with greater structural complexity, such as Bi LSTM combined with contextual attention, showed reduced accuracy and higher variance. The findings demonstrate that appropriately designed hybrid deep learning models can effectively capture complex temporal patterns in diesel generator behaviour. These results highlight the potential of hybrid deep learning approaches to support data driven optimisation of shipboard energy management and contribute to more efficient and sustainable vessel operations.

title: THE REGULATORY ARCHITECTURE OF LEGAL AI: BAR AUTHORITY, FEDERAL PREEMPTION, AND THE GOVERNANCE GAP
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: THE REGULATORY ARCHITECTURE OF LEGAL AI: BAR AUTHORITY, FEDERAL PREEMPTION, AND THE GOVERNANCE GAP
detail.abstract:
Federal courts and state bars have produced fundamentally incompatible regulatory regimes governing attorney use of artificial intelligence. More than three hundred federal court standing orders now address AI-assisted filings, ranging from mandatory disclosure to outright bans. More than forty-seven state bar ethics opinions, anchored by ABA Formal Opinion 512, permit AI use subject to competence, confidentiality, candor, and supervision obligations. Executive Order 14,365, issued in December 2025, directed the Department of Justice to challenge state AI laws as preempted by federal authority. Practitioners face contradictory commands from three separate regulatory layers, and no existing institutional architecture resolves the conflict.

This Article develops two substantive targets that any coherent regulatory architecture for legal AI must enforce. The first target is a certification regime calibrated to what AI systems must do: a certainty-threshold framework operating per task class, per architectural tier, and per stake, drawing on the architectural-tier taxonomy and AI Legal Reference Model developed in prior papers in this series. The second target is an antecedent permission layer addressing whether a particular use is permitted at all, operationalized at the platform layer through role-based access control governing supervisory authority, attribute-based access control enforcing per-call operational authority, and federated agentic identity protocols enabling cross-organizational AI agent interaction without compromising privilege or confidentiality. Certification asks whether the tool is adequate; authority to process asks whether the use is permitted at all.

The institutional allocation through which these targets are enforced forms a three-legged regulatory architecture. State bars retain primary authority over the ethical dimensions of attorney AI use under bar federalism and the Middlesex presumption. Federal courts retain authority over procedural requirements for AI-assisted filings under the Rules Enabling Act and inherent supervisory power. Federal legislation governs vendor regulation through a framework mirroring the three historical preemption models analyzed in this Article: SOX § 307 / Part 205, the McDade Amendment, and IRS Circular 230. The Allocation Principle resolves the regulatory trilemma without displacing state bar authority or producing federal preemption without replacement.

The Article identifies five governance gaps the current architecture cannot resolve, develops a falsifiable five-year prediction across three regulatory configurations with probability weights, and supplies practitioner action items, regulator amendment templates, and a federal vendor-regulation framework. The proposed architecture is structurally compatible with the solo-practitioner segment of the bar through a lowest-common-denominator design constraint.

title: Optical Waveguides Constructed from Recycled Expanded Polystyrene (EPS) and Their Properties
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Optical Waveguides Constructed from Recycled Expanded Polystyrene (EPS) and Their Properties
detail.abstract: In an effort to develop a more environmentally friendly method to fabricating photonic devices, this research investigated the feasibility of using recycled expanded polystyrene (EPS) as the primary material for optical waveguides. The optical characteristics of expanded polystyrene were investigated in this study, as were the effects of the recycling process, which involves heating the material in a furnace for two hours at temperatures between 200 and 280 degrees Celsius. According to the refractive index results, the optimal temperatures for expanded polystyrene to be used in waveguide applications are 200 °C (EPS200) and 210 °C (EPS210). The waveguides were built using recycled expanded polystyrene, with grooves carved to 1 × 1 mm² by a CNC machine and filled with polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) as cladding. Measurements of the operating temperature range, propagation loss, temperature-dependent loss, and time-dependent stability were conducted during characterization. The EPS200 and EPS210 waveguides were found to offer the best combination of low power loss, stable propagation, acceptable temperature-dependent loss values, and operational reliability up to 60 °C. Based on these results, it seems that waveguides made of recycled expanded polystyrene might help promote more environmentally friendly production practices and green photonic device research and development.

title: The International AI Accountability Forum 2026: Architecting the Jurisprudential Foundation for Enforceable AI Accountability in the Age of Agentic Intelligence
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The International AI Accountability Forum 2026: Architecting the Jurisprudential Foundation for Enforceable AI Accountability in the Age of Agentic Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares the following matters in the interest of full scholarly transparency. The author is the originator of the Duggal Doctrine of Ten Common Legal Principles for AI Regulation, the Duggal Global Agentic AI Liability Framework, the concept of Sovereign AI Accountability, and the related doctrinal contributions advanced in this paper. The work was conducted independently by the author and supported institutionally by Pavan Duggal Associates, Advocates, the Global Artificial Intelligence Law and Governance Institute (GAILGI), and the Artificial Intelligence Law Hub. detail.abstract:
The international community stands at a defining jurisprudential moment. Artificial Intelligence systems, and increasingly, autonomous agentic AI architectures, have outpaced the regulatory imagination of every legal order on the planet. Existing instruments, whether the European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act, the patchwork of executive directives in the United States, China's algorithmic recommendation regulations, or India's amended Information Technology Intermediary Rules of February 2026, address fragments of the AI accountability problem. None has yet established a coherent, globally portable, enforceable architecture of AI accountability anchored in equity for the Global South. 

This working paper introduces and frames the International AI Accountability Forum (IAAF) convened at New Delhi in 2026. The Forum advances the jurisprudential mission inaugurated by the New Delhi Accord on AI and Emerging Tech Law of 24 July 2025 and operationalizes the Duggal Doctrine of Ten Common Legal Principles for AI Regulation. The Forum proposes and develops the AI Accountability Framework, 2026 as also Duggal Global Agentic AI Liability Framework as the first comprehensive multi-actor liability doctrine specifically designed for autonomous AI agents. The paper proceeds in six parts. Part I diagnoses the global accountability moment. Part II examines the inadequacy of existing frameworks. Part III locates the IAAF within the doctrinal arc inaugurated by GSAIET 2025. Part IV sets out the operative content of the Duggal Doctrine of Ten Principles. Part V develops the agentic AI liability problem, the multi-actor liability cascade, and the question of AI legal personhood. Part VI concludes with the civilizational imperative of AI accountability and a forward-looking treaty roadmap toward 2030. 

The central thesis is that AI accountability is not optional; it is the jurisprudential imperative of the twenty-first century. The IAAF is offered as the convening institution through which this imperative becomes enforceable law.
