detail.title: Temporal Coherence in Artificial Intelligence Systems: A Unified Policy Framework for Training Compute Allocation, Inference Serving, and User Engagement Under Synchronized Demand
detail.abstract: There is a cost inside every major AI platform that does not appear on any infrastructure dashboard. When a model launch, a viral moment, or a deadline-driven traffic spike causes GPU inference queues to overflow, users do not simply wait. They cancel. They immediately retry. Each retry consumes fresh compute on an already-saturated system. The retry rate is not constant-it rises.

title: The Geometric Siphon: Existence, Equilibrium, and Directional Properties of the Residual in Concentrated Liquidity Portfolios
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Geometric Siphon: Existence, Equilibrium, and Directional Properties of the Residual in Concentrated Liquidity Portfolios
detail.abstract: This paper identifies and formalises the Geometric Siphon, a previously undocumented mechanism arising from concentrated-liquidity rebalancing geometry and made observable across positions by shared depositor balances. When autonomously rebalanced positions share a token balance, token-ratio mismatches between old and new tick ranges route residual tokens through that shared balance, transferring capital between positions in independent pools. Six theorems characterise the mechanism. They establish a closed-form residual with an iff vanishing condition, convergence in expectation for same-pool positions sharing a contract balance, and geometric extinction without swap correction. On volatile/stablecoin pairs in V3 ordering, they also establish strict residual monotonicity in displacement together with USD-denominated directional and exit asymmetries. A graph-theoretic Connector Rule relating per-pool flow to portfolio topology is stated as a conjecture. A 16-test Foundry suite verifies all six theorems against unmodified V3 contracts on Base mainnet. Empirically, a 1,380-event controlled dataset is consistent with the existence claim, contains a complete USDC/ZARP extinction lifecycle, and includes an observed single-pool convergence episode. A separate 35,910-event productionscale dataset spanning five independent portfolios replicates the directional asymmetry in every portfolio, the exit asymmetry in four of five, and exhibits the predicted sign flip in the largest portfolio's reversed-ordering negative control.

title: Lender Not Out To Make Borrower Insolvent’: An Insight Into The Terms Of A Term Loan Agreement, Its Purpose And Legal Effect

detail.title: Lender Not Out To Make Borrower Insolvent’: An Insight Into The Terms Of A Term Loan Agreement, Its Purpose And Legal Effect
detail.abstract: A loan between a lender and a borrower made for duration with a specified (fixed) maturity date is classified as a term loan. It is a loan between the lender on the one part and the borrower on the other part whereby the lender advance funds to the borrower within a time limit with the payment of interest subject to condition precedents which includes representations, warranties and covenants made by the borrower to the lender, and subject to a breach of any such condition precedent, the lender has a right of terminating the term loan agreement by stopping advance of any more funds to the borrower and claiming repayment of the funds already advanced to the borrower. However, the borrower may elect to prepay the term loan. There are instances where prepayment may become compulsory for the borrower. For instance, in a situation where the term loan advanced becomes illegal under the Laws of the country of the lender or where there is a change of control in the borrowing company or where the company is transferred to another owner who do not want to continue with the loan agreement or even in the case of a ‘cash sweep’ where the borrower is generating interest than they envisaged. However, it is trite law that a loan advanced to a borrower has a specified payment period and must be repaid at the end of that period. Repayment under an amortization design may be a ‘lump sum repayment’, a ‘balloon repayment’, or a ‘scheduled repayment’. All repayment comes with interest which is a source of profit to the lender. It covers cost, for example documentation fee for the lender and also compensates the lender for risk of default by the borrower and even early repayment. Early repayment (prepayment) which is as a result of a change of control at the borrower’s company may be classified as a prepayment at the borrower’s will than out of the borrower’s will because the new management at the borrower’s company helms of affair may decide to ratify the term loan agreement and then repay according to the schedule between the lender and the borrower. Though this is subject to ratification under the Law of Agency, although the borrower would have breached representation made to the lender, however the lender is not out to make the borrower insolvent. A term loan in essence can be a fixed repayment schedule.

title: « Bill shock » : Consumer protection issues and controversies between regulators, operators and mobile phone subscribers
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: « Bill shock » : Consumer protection issues and controversies between regulators, operators and mobile phone subscribers
detail.abstract: This document first presents the main measures protecting mobile phone consumers against excessive bills, commonly known as "bill shock," in force since 2005 in both Belgium and Europe. These mechanisms, defined primarily by the European Union (EU) as well as those proposed in Belgium by the BIPT (Belgian Institute for Postal Services and Telecommunications) in the amendment to the law adopted after 2020, are analysed and discussed in the body of the text. The document then highlights operator practices, consumer behaviour, and their evolution from 2005 to the present day. In Belgium, in 2026, overage charges still persist when consumers do not choose an operator offering an overage protection option, when such an option exists. Operators are not fully transparent: they often steer customers toward unsuitable plans and fail to promote the protections they should be recommending. To date, less than half of Belgian operators offer an overage protection option. Other operators continue to practice out-of-plan charges, an approach that offers little security for consumers and which more information and education could change in the coming years. The safest measure is to automatically block the plan as soon as a limit on calls, SMS, or mobile data is reached. Finally, a qualitative comparison of current operator offers is presented to help readers choose the most suitable plan. "Bill shock" should soon disappear in Belgium, as well as for roaming in Europe, thanks to the "Roam Like at Home" law, which has been in effect since June 2027.

title: There is More to Crowdshipping Than Money: Understanding how Operational Characteristics Influence Driver Behaviors
affiliations: , Independent, University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Anderson School of Management and University of Arkansas

detail.title: There is More to Crowdshipping Than Money: Understanding how Operational Characteristics Influence Driver Behaviors

contentType.other: Accepted for Publication in the Journal of Operations Management

detail.abstract: The increasing cost of last-mile delivery has motivated omnichannel grocery retailers to implement crowdshipping. Crowdshipping is a platform-based last-mile delivery model that relies on engaging drivers who are independent contractors to quickly accept delivery tasks. While studies often focus on the impact of monetary incentives, we draw on perspectives from the service operations literature to explore the moderating effect of three theoretical mechanisms (effort efficiency, uncertainty, and utility), on the curvilinear relationship between monetary incentives and driver engagement. Specifically, we test how delivery density, delivery type (attended vs unattended), and time of the day interact with monetary incentives to influence driver's task acceptance response time. Econometric analyses of a dataset comprising about two million observations from a U.S. Fortune 100 grocery retailer's crowdshipping platform confirm the "diminishing negative" effect of remuneration on task acceptance time. More importantly, we reveal that task operational characteristics affect how monetary incentives influence task acceptance time. While task density and unattended deliveries amplify the curvilinear relationship, evening tasks flatten it and are accepted slower than those scheduled in the daytime. Our findings suggest that drivers evaluate tasks based on perceived effort, uncertainty, and utility, offering valuable insights for platforms and future research.

title: Opening the Black Box: Operational Principles, Tools and Frameworks That Advance Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) Models
affiliations: University of Malta

detail.title: Opening the Black Box: Operational Principles, Tools and Frameworks That Advance Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) Models
detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) models are increasingly becoming permeated across various domains, there are instances where they are generating hallucinations, misinformation and erroneous outputs. Various stakeholders, particularly the regulatory ones, are encouraging the developers of machine learning (ML) systems to clarify or justify their models' decisions, actions or predictions in a way that is understandable to their users. In this light, this article raises awareness on Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) principles that are intended to increase transparency, accountability and fairness about the modus operandi of machine learning algorithms. A systematic review of the extant literature identifies key tools, frameworks and best practices that enhance the interpretability of AI models, including open-source techniques like SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), among others. The synthesis of the findings also shed light on XAI challenges and limitations of black-box models. This contribution advances a conceptual framework for the responsible implementation of XAI and offers practical guidelines that promote the interpretability of AI systems, whilst addressing their opacity, as well as their biased outcomes. It puts forward theoretical and managerial implications as well as future research avenues.

title: Human Viability Diagnostic Framework for Advanced AI (HVDFAI)

detail.title: Human Viability Diagnostic Framework for Advanced AI (HVDFAI)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, personal data, or ethical approval requirements.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The widespread adoption of generative AI has produced an extensive literature on the human capabilities required to work effectively alongside intelligent systems. This literature converges on lists of desirable soft skills-critical thinking, resilience, creativity-without explaining why these capacities become necessary at a specific point in the human-AI interaction, or which operational conditions determine whether a human can sustain that interaction once the system stops behaving predictably. This paper addresses that gap. We propose the Human Viability Diagnostic Framework for Advanced AI (HVDFAI), a conceptual framework developed through inductive practitioner research across hundreds of real interaction cycles with large language model systems. The framework makes two original contributions.

title: Analytical regulation mapping for cooling-water flow in coal-fired condensers under electricity spot-market price signals
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and North China Electric Power University

detail.title: Analytical regulation mapping for cooling-water flow in coal-fired condensers under electricity spot-market price signals
detail.abstract: The expansion of electricity spot markets with frequent negative-price intervals reshapes the economic value of cooling-water flow adjustments in coal-fired condensers operating under deep peak shaving. This work develops an analytical regulation framework based on fundamental condenser energy balance. A closed-form heat-exchange margin is established to quantify feasible flow boundaries, and a marginal-response ratio is derived to characterize the continuous transition between hydraulic-dominated and thermal-dominated regimes. Integrating these two indicators with real-time price polarity yields a four-zone operational regulation diagram that analytically depicts optimal decisions across the zero-price threshold. Validation on a 630 MW coal-fired unit in the Zhejiang electricity spot market shows that the four-zone strategy matches full-enumeration optimization within a 0.5% error margin while reducing online computation by over an order of magnitude. The proposed framework provides a generalizable analytical approach for auxiliary system dispatch under negative-price conditions.

title: Will Mounting Supply Chain Strains Hamstring the AI Investment Boom?
affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of New York and Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of New York

detail.title: Will Mounting Supply Chain Strains Hamstring the AI Investment Boom?

publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
The conflict in the Middle East has precipitated a global supply shock—the third in six years following the pandemic in 2020 and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The current shock raises the specter of spillovers to the U.S. through both prices and physical shortages of goods. A critical conduit for spillovers through these channels is via Asian supply chains, especially from middle- to lower-middle income countries in southeast Asia, which are key suppliers for goods needed for the AI infrastructure build-out in the U.S. These countries are also heavily reliant on Middle East energy imports. This post examines key factors related to these Asian supply chain vulnerabilities.

To view post: https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2026/05/will-mounting-supply-chain-strains-hamstring-the-ai-investment-boom/

title: Direct cooling heat transfer enhancement and temperature control strategy optimization for commercial lithium-ion battery energy storage systems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Qingdao University of Technology, Qingdao University of Technology, Qingdao University of Technology, Tsinghua University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Direct cooling heat transfer enhancement and temperature control strategy optimization for commercial lithium-ion battery energy storage systems
detail.abstract: During frequency regulation and peak shaving in energy storage stations, heat accumulation within lithium-ion battery systems degrades temperature field uniformity, subsequently impairing their service life and performance. Recently, direct refrigerant cooling has attracted widespread attention in lithium-ion battery thermal management due to its superior heat transfer efficiency, which leverages the latent heat of gas-liquid phase change. However, since lithium-ion battery systems in energy storage applications adopt a vertically stacked configuration, the gravitational field induces maldistribution in the two-phase refrigerant flow, which compromises the uniform temperature control of the batteries. Consequently, this study investigates direct cooling heat transfer enhancement and temperature control strategy optimization for a 186.4 kWh large-capacity commercial lithium-ion battery energy storage system, analyzing the mechanism by which gas-liquid two-phase distribution affects temperature uniformity under gravity with a focus on piping network design. Initially, Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is employed to comparatively analyze the connection configurations of cold plate flow channels across 10 distinct direct cooling piping network designs. The results indicate that the "All-Series 1" design effectively limits the maximum temperature of the battery cluster to 32.2 °C, with a maximum temperature difference of 3.8 °C. Subsequently, the NSGA-II algorithm combined with the TOPSIS method is utilized for objective decision-making to establish the optimal temperature control strategy. The findings reveal that under a 0.5P constant power discharge condition, the optimal operating parameters are a refrigerant mass flow rate of 0.05 kg/s and an inlet temperature of 18.12 °C. Compared to the baseline condition (mass flow rate of 0.025 kg/s, inlet temperature of 18 °C), the maximum temperature difference is reduced to 3.45 °C, representing a 9.2% decrease. By focusing on direct refrigerant cooling in commercial energy storage systems, this study proposes an optimized piping network design and temperature control strategy, providing a robust theoretical foundation and technical reference for thermal management and temperature uniformity enhancement in energy storage applications.

title: From the Editors: Engaged Scholarship in International Business Policy - Strengthening Policy Contributions
affiliations: Newcastle University, , The University of Manchester - Manchester Business School and University of Leeds - Faculty of Business

detail.title: From the Editors: Engaged Scholarship in International Business Policy - Strengthening Policy Contributions
detail.abstract: This editorial advances recent efforts to define and strengthen international business policy research. Building on Van Assche and De Marchi’s (2024) discussion of the boundaries of IB policy research and De Marchi et al.’s (2025) guidance on crafting articles that resonate with policy actors, we ask how different forms of policy contribution can be articulated, positioned, and assessed. We introduce a policy contribution pyramid, anchored in the policy design cycle, as a classificatory tool for authors, reviewers, and editors. The pyramid identifies five domains: policy insight and problem framing; policy instruments and instrumentation; policy mix design, learning, and adaptation; policy process insight; and policy agenda navigation strategy. Together, these domains provide a shared vocabulary for clarifying policy problems, refining individual instruments, analysing how instruments work together, explaining how policy decisions and implementation unfold, and interpreting how agendas, narratives, and coalitions evolve. The editorial argues that policy-relevant IB research does not always need to offer direct recommendations. Articles may contribute by improving how a policy problem is framed, showing how an instrument operates in practice, analysing the evolution of policy mixes, or explaining why implementation differs from policymakers’ intentions. The policy contribution pyramid is therefore not limited to engaged scholarship; it can also help position conceptual, qualitative, and quantitative studies by clarifying what kind of policy contribution they make and how they relate to the policy process.

title: DIR-GNN: A Dynamic Incremental Robust Graph Neural Network Resource Allocation Method for High-Dynamic Industrial Networks
affiliations: Hefei University of Technology and Hefei University of Technology

detail.title: DIR-GNN: A Dynamic Incremental Robust Graph Neural Network Resource Allocation Method for High-Dynamic Industrial Networks

keywords.keywords: Dynamic Graph Neural Network Incremental LearningAdversarial Robustness Resource AllocationIndustrial Wireless Control Network Routing and Spectrum Allocation

detail.abstract: Industrial wireless control networks face a dual challenge of concurrent channel resource scarcity and severe electromagnetic interference when handling mixed traffic flows: high-priority deterministic traffic (e.g., motion control, secure parking) and low-priority elastic traffic (e.g., video surveillance). Existing resource allocation schemes based on static graph neural networks (GNN) struggle to simultaneously address three critical challenges: rapid topology changes, intense interference, and limited edge computing capabilities. This paper proposes the Dynamic Incremental Robust Graph Neural Network (DIRGNN), which restructures the perception and decision-making processes through three core mechanisms: incremental graph updates perform recomputation only on locally affected subgraphs during topology changes, fundamentally eliminating global retraining overhead; an adversarial training hardening model based on projected gradient descent enhances robustness against observation noise; and adaptive lightweight compression integrates deep separable convolutional architectures, learnable pruning masks, and quantization-aware training to enable flexible deployment of edge controllers. The model simultaneously outputs fine-grained Quality of Service (QoS) metrics—including link quality, traffic trends, fault risk probabilities, latency, and jitter—and interacts with SDN controllers via standardized JSON messages to directly drive proactive routing and spectrum allocation strategies informed by fragment awareness. At the methodological level, DirGNN explicitly defines interface primitives between its engine and OpenFlow controllers, seamlessly integrating intelligent perception into the closed-loop industrial deterministic network scheduling framework. The model is evaluated against 11 baseline approaches across three distinct dynamic scenarios—including mine simulations, NSFNET, and GEANT—covering pure time-series models, static GNNs, spatiotemporal GNNs, incremental GNNs, and online learning strategies. Experimental results demonstrate that DIRGNN reduces the link quality prediction mean square error (MSE) by over 34%, lowers the blocking rate to 4.2%, optimizes latency and jitter by 28% and 35% respectively, while cutting the total number of model parameters by 42%. Comparison of fine-grained incremental strategies highlights the synergistic benefits of local recomputation and empirical replay; edge deployment experiments generated continuous resource latency accuracy curves, validating the effectiveness of dynamic bandwidth selection for real-time inference; in simplified TSN scenarios, the prediction-driven pre-switching mechanism reduces fault recovery latency by 72%, with deterministic flows meeting the 1 ms latency threshold 99.9% of the time. This work provides a model-driven, standards-compatible, interface-defined, and deployable intelligent resource management solution for demanding industrial environments.

title:
Why Innovation Fails in Well-Run Companies--
The Selection-Before-Evolution Trap
affiliations: Fan Ge Institute

detail.title:
Why Innovation Fails in Well-Run Companies--
The Selection-Before-Evolution Trap
detail.abstract:
This paper examines why innovation often fails in well-run organizations. It introduces the concept of the selection-before-evolution trap, arguing that early-stage ideas are frequently eliminated not due to lack of potential, but because they are evaluated using the performance criteria of mature business operations.
The paper distinguishes between core logic (focused on efficiency and predictability) and frontier logic (focused on learning and uncertainty reduction), and proposes a practical framework—the Corporate Evolution Dashboard—to help organizations align evaluation mechanisms with the stage of innovation.
By shifting the focus from execution to selection mechanisms, this work provides a structural explanation for innovation failure and offers guidance for designing conditions under which new ideas can survive long enough to evolve.

title: Institutional sources of cooperation, competition and conflict in developing countries: the cases of civil service administration in Afghanistan and PNG
affiliations: The Australian National University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Institutional sources of cooperation, competition and conflict in developing countries: the cases of civil service administration in Afghanistan and PNG
detail.abstract: Institutions are central to political life, yet institutional dysfunctionality remains endemic in many developing countries. In postcolonial settings, institutions inherited through decolonisation have often proved inappropriate to new states, either because of mismatches between institutional form and long-standing authority patterns or because these legacy institutions created incentives for destructive behaviours. These problems are not confined to the postcolonial space, but have also appeared in contexts of multilateral state-building and institutional design. This paper examines how institutional design can incentivise cooperation, competition, or conflict by analysing cases of civil service administration in Afghanistan between 2001 and 2021 and in Papua New Guinea after independence in 1975. It argues that a neutral, politically impartial civil service is itself a political objective, but that institutional design has not been able to overcome broader social and political incentives fostering patronage and networking. Careful reflection is therefore required before new arrangements are put in place.

title: Optimizing Batch Size in Three-Echelon Supply Chains with Multi-Supplier Integration, Multistage Parallel Production, and Multi-Distributor Networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Mapúa University - School of Industrial Engineering and Engineering Management

detail.title: Optimizing Batch Size in Three-Echelon Supply Chains with Multi-Supplier Integration, Multistage Parallel Production, and Multi-Distributor Networks
detail.abstract: Modern supply chains face persistent cost and service inefficiencies due to misaligned incentives across suppliers, manufacturers, and distributors. This paper develops a deterministic, single-period model for a three-echelon supply chain that jointly optimizes quantity-based wholesale price discounts and transportation cost-sharing within a multistage parallel-production and multi-distributor framework. Built on an EOQ-derived foundation, the model minimizes total system cost via a composite function covering purchasing, ordering, multi-stage inventory holding (raw materials, work-in-process, finished goods), inbound freight net of supplier reimbursements, plant setup and processing costs, and outbound transportation via hybrid full-truckload and less-than-truckload services. The resulting optimization landscape is mixed-integer nonlinear due to piecewise discount structures, binary shipment-mode decisions, and integer truck counts. It is solved with four tailored metaheuristics: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Ant Colony Optimization (ACOR-variant), and Simulated Annealing (SA), implementing problem-specific encodings, constraint-handling operators, and tuned parameters. Tested on an industrial HDPE case with two raw-material suppliers, a three-stage parallel production system, and two distributors, 32 independent runs per algorithm show strong feasibility-driven bimodality: only 88 runs achieve full feasibility (zero-penalty). Among feasible outcomes, ACOR is most reliable (70%) and efficient, converging to near-optimal ≈$5.64 million solutions; GA reaches 30% reliability; PSO matches quality inconsistently; SA finds none. The optimal policy eliminates penalties via large-batch, fewer-cycles strategy with 6-7% discounts, 13-25% reimbursements, and hybrid TL/LTL maximizing full-truckload use

title: LSTM–Transformer Autoencoder for Anomaly Detection: Application to a Real-World Multimode Industrial Chemical Process
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Aalborg University, Kyung Hee University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: LSTM–Transformer Autoencoder for Anomaly Detection: Application to a Real-World Multimode Industrial Chemical Process
detail.abstract: Modern chemical processes comprise multiple interconnected unit operations with complex dependencies, in which even minor faults can lead to product loss, quality degradation, energy waste, resource loss, and environmental pollution. These issues can be mitigated through anomaly-detection models, which enable early detection of abnormal process conditions and timely corrective actions. However, conventional statistical and data-driven fault-detection methods often assume that the process is either static or governed by simple dynamics, thus failing to adequately capture the nonlinear and high-dimensional characteristics of real-world industrial systems. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel anomaly-detection framework called the LSTM–transformer autoencoder (LTAE). The model employs a long short-term memory (LSTM) encoder to effectively capture dynamic temporal changes in the process data, and a transformer-based decoder with multi-head attention learns long-range dependencies and critical information in parallel to achieve precise reconstruction. When applied to the Tennessee Eastman (TE) benchmark process under a single-mode setting, the proposed model maintained a low false alarm rate (FAR) of 0.00, similar to the baseline models, while enhancing the fault detection rate (FDR) from 0.83 to 0.86. Furthermore, in a multimode setting using a real-world industrial polyethylene (PE) production process, the model significantly reduced the FAR from 0.85 (dual-attention LSTM, transformer) to 0.05, while sustaining an FDR of 1.00. These results demonstrate that the proposed model delivers robust anomaly detection performance in both single- and multimode environments, serving as a practical solution to minimize resource waste, reduce unnecessary energy consumption, and mitigate environmental risks.

title: Beyond Multi-Stage Pipelines: End-to-End Analog Gauge Reading via Specialized Vision-Language Models
affiliations: University of Central Florida, University of Central Florida, University of Central Florida, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Central Florida

detail.title: Beyond Multi-Stage Pipelines: End-to-End Analog Gauge Reading via Specialized Vision-Language Models
detail.abstract: While industrial automation is accelerating, the persistence of legacy analog gauges necessitates robust, automated monitoring solutions to ensure operational safety and data continuity. This paper presents an end-to-end framework for robust analog gauge reading by specializing the Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct vision-language model (VLM) for high-precision industrial metrology. We systematically benchmark the transition from general-purpose foundation model to specialized industrial tool across zero-shot, in-context learning (ICL), and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies. Evaluations are conducted on three diverse datasets: a public synthetic collection, a video-derived benchmark, and a proprietary real-world industrial dataset featuring complex environmental conditions. Our findings demonstrate that while foundational VLMs lack the inherent zero-shot reliability required for industrial standards, PEFT using Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA) transforms the model into a high-precision regressor. The specialized model achieves a Mean Percentage Error (MPE) between 1.93% and 3.4%, significantly outperforming traditional multi-stage computer vision pipelines and smaller VLM architectures. We further analyze the model's sensitivity to explicit scale parameters and identify a critical ‘perceptual-cognitive disconnect’ where the model exhibits high-confidence failure modes despite correct visual attention. These results provide a roadmap for integrating large-scale foundation models into autonomous industrial inspection frameworks while highlighting the necessity for external uncertainty quantification in safety-critical deployments.

title: Single-Source Splitting Domain Adaptation for Container Rehandling Probability Prediction
affiliations: Tongji University, Tongji University, Tongji University and Tongji University

detail.title: Single-Source Splitting Domain Adaptation for Container Rehandling Probability Prediction
detail.abstract: The container rehandling probability prediction model based on deep learning can assist the formulation of container storage strategies for reducing the rehandling container rate in the port. However, the actual storage situation of container within the yard and the potential rehandling relation hidden in container storage sequence are often divergent across different ports, thus roughly constructing a universal prediction model struggles to deliver consistent, high-quality inference performance across different ports, significantly undermining the generalization capacity of prediction model. To address the above issue, we proposed a novel single-source splitting domain adaptation(S3DA) to enhance the inference performance of the container rehandling probability prediction model on smallscale container storage sequences of target port, thereby advancing the generalization application of the prediction model across ports. S3DA has three distinctive characteristics: (i) Container storage sequence data augmentation, which expands the sample number of the target domain and enriches the diversity of the target domain data, alleviating the issue of insufficient target domain data. (ii) Domain segmentation operation splits the source domain into multiple sub-source domains that more closely resemble the data distribution of the target domain, facilitating knowledge transfer from the source domain to the target domain. (iii) The tier matching mechanism guides the prediction model to learn cross-tier invariant feature representations, balancing the inference performance of the prediction model across different tiers of containers. The evaluation outcomes demonstrate the performance and practical values of the proposed S3DA approach.

title: Seismic Performance Degradation Variability Analysis of Long-Span Suspension Bridge with Leaking Viscous Dampers
affiliations: Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Dalian University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Seismic Performance Degradation Variability Analysis of Long-Span Suspension Bridge with Leaking Viscous Dampers
detail.abstract: Viscous dampers in long-span suspension bridges frequently suffer from medium leakage during long-term service, which severely restricts their energy dissipation capacity and threatens structural safety. Existing studies predominantly rely on intact damper models, failing to capture the equivalent empty stroke effect induced by leakage and ignoring the robustness differences of design parameters during the degradation process. To address this, this paper investigates the seismic response of suspension bridges under damper degradation. An equivalent mechanical model integrating damping, gap, and hook elements is proposed and verified to simulate the leakage mechanism. Taking a suspension bridge with a 1385 m main span as an example, the structural response and damper performance under varying leakage levels are evaluated under seismic loads. Furthermore, a joint response surface analysis focusing on the highly sensitive girder end displacement is conducted to explore the robustness against degradation robustness of the damping coefficient and velocity exponent across different leakage stages. The results reveal that damper leakage significantly exacerbates girder end displacement but exerts a minor effect on structural internal forces. A strong nonlinear interaction exists between the design parameters and the leakage severity, meaning the dominant parameter governing the damping effectiveness shifts as degradation deepens. Performance deterioration accelerates significantly in advanced leakage stages, and the robustness of different parameter configurations varies distinctly depending on the leakage stage. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the condition assessment, parameter optimization, and life-cycle maintenance of viscous dampers.

title: Accelerating AC-Feasible Unit Commitment via Global Model Updates and Local Constraint Corrections
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, The Hang Seng University of Hong Kong, The University of Hong Kong and The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Accelerating AC-Feasible Unit Commitment via Global Model Updates and Local Constraint Corrections
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a GL-ACUC correction mechanism for AC unit commitment (ACUC) under the master surrogate UC problem--AC feasibility check subproblem paradigm. The master surrogate UC problem uses a linear network surrogate built from Taylor-expanded AC power flow equations together with polygon-based approximations of line-flow limits, and the AC feasibility check subproblem validates candidate commitment and dispatch schedules on the full AC network. To improve model fidelity without repeatedly destabilizing the mixed-integer feasible region, we coordinate two complementary correction actions within the GL-ACUC correction mechanism. The global model update refreshes the reference operating state and recomputes the associated Jacobian information to enhance global consistency between the linear surrogate and AC physics. The local constraints correction then repairs residual AC violations through targeted limit tightening, providing fine-grained feasibility adjustments with minimal disturbance to the master surrogate UC problem structure. Case studies on the IEEE 57-bus benchmark system demonstrate that the proposed GL-ACUC correction mechanism reduces linearization errors and constraint violations, improves AC feasibility and convergence stability, and achieves lower operating cost with fewer outer iterations than the baseline linear surrogate.

title: Systematic Comparison of Transmission Grid Reduction Methods for Congestion Management Modeling: Voltage Level Scope and Spatial Clustering for Germany
affiliations: Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt

detail.title: Systematic Comparison of Transmission Grid Reduction Methods for Congestion Management Modeling: Voltage Level Scope and Spatial Clustering for Germany
detail.abstract: Modeling congestion management in transmission systems involves significant challenges due to high computational requirements and uncertainties in grid parameters as well as in the spatial allocation of demand and generation. Grid reduction methods are therefore increasingly applied to simplify grid representations while preserving relevant system characteristics. However, their impact on congestion management modeling results has not yet been systematically assessed. This study addresses this gap by analyzing the influence of grid reduction methods and grid level scope on congestion management modeling using a case study for Germany.Based on the open-source framework PyPSA-Eur, 15 grid configurations are developed across three scenario levels: (i) inclusion or exclusion of the high voltage (HV) grid, (ii) aggregation of HV into the extra-high voltage (EHV) level, and (iii) application of spatial clustering algorithms. All configurations are calibrated for 2019 and validated against historical congestion management data using topological indicators as well as redispatch volumes and their regional distribution.Results show that full-resolution HV grid representations without reduction lead to implausibly high redispatch volumes. In contrast, combining HV grid reduction with spatial clustering improves the spatial representation of congestion management and yields more plausible redispatch patterns. Differences between clustering algorithms remain minor when consistent clustering features and connectivity constraints are applied. Despite these improvements, all scenarios still overestimate historical redispatch volumes, with the closest match exceeding them by a factor of 2.26.Overall, the findings highlight the importance of appropriate grid level scope and reduction strategies for reliable congestion management modeling under uncertain input conditions.

title: Examining the Growing Movement to Grant Antitrust Exemptions for Coordinated Behavior
affiliations: George Mason University - Antonin Scalia Law School

detail.title: Examining the Growing Movement to Grant Antitrust Exemptions for Coordinated Behavior
detail.abstract:
This article examines the growing movement among legislators and competition authorities to create antitrust exemptions for coordinated conduct among competitors when such coordination is said to advance broader public policy goals, including environmental sustainability and journalism preservation. Using examples from the United States and Europe, the article explores the tension between traditional antitrust principles—which have long condemned collusion and price fixing—and emerging public-interest approaches to antitrust.

Specifically, this article advances that these exemptions create significant legal and economic risks. In particular, the boundaries of permissible coordination are difficult to define and enforce, exemptions may generate unintended market distortions and rent-seeking behavior, and selectively permitting collusion risks undermining the coherence and legitimacy of antitrust law. The article concludes that special carve-outs are unnecessary because antitrust law already accommodates genuinely procompetitive cooperation under the existing rule of reason framework.

title: Extended Warranties as a Regressive Cross-Subsidy
affiliations: University of Minnesota - Law School and UC Law, San Francisco

detail.title: Extended Warranties as a Regressive Cross-Subsidy

publicationDetails.detailsText: Minnesota Legal Studies Research Paper No. 2026-28
publicationDetails.journalName: University of Minnesota Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper examines optional product insurance-such as extended warranties, device protection plans, and embedded service contracts-as a regressive cross-subsidy. Standard accounts treat these add-ons as optional risk-transfer contracts. We argue that they also perform a price-structuring function. When demand for optional insurance declines with income, firms can recover part of the product price through higher insurance premiums paid by lower-income consumers. Higher-income consumers are more likely to opt out and self-insure, benefiting from lower product prices without bearing the insurance margin. Optional insurance can therefore raise the effective price paid by lower-income consumers while lowering the base price paid by higherincome uninsured consumers. The paper explores the effects of this mechanism within a law-andeconomics framework that connects risk allocation, price discrimination, and distributional effects. It distinguishes the cross-subsidy effects from adverse selection. Under adverse selection, premiums rise because the insured pool becomes riskier. Under the cross-subsidy account, premiums may rise even when the risk pool remains stable, because firms can extract higher premiums from consumers with greater willingness to pay for coverage. The distinction matters for policy. Adverse selection points toward information remedies and risk classification; crosssubsidization points toward closer scrutiny of multi-part pricing and the possible role of mandatory baseline coverage. The analysis thus offers a distributional rationale for mandatory legal warranties, such as EU-style consumer protection mandates, as a way to limit regressive transfers made possible by optional insurance markets.

title: The Fragmentation of Insecurity

detail.title: The Fragmentation of Insecurity
detail.abstract: Nigeria's security crisis is routinely framed through a singular religious lens, most prominently as a campaign of systematic persecution against Christians. This paper challenges that framing as empirically insufficient and politically dangerous. Drawing on disaggregated fatality data, conflict typologies, and structural governance analysis, the paper argues that Nigeria's insecurity is fundamentally a consequence of state failure, elite manipulation, climate-induced resource scarcity, and institutional impunity, all of which cut across religious and ethnic lines with lethal indifference. The evidence reveals three interlocking conflict systems: jihadist insurgency (primarily Boko Haram and ISWAP), resource-based communal violence concentrated in the Middle Belt, and profit-driven organised criminality. Between 2006 and 2021, crime-related violence alone caused approximately 51,425 deaths, marginally exceeding the 50,252 fatalities attributed to terrorist insurgency. Data from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED) further confirms that between 2020 and 2025, attacks targeting Muslims resulted in at least 418 deaths, compared to 318 deaths from attacks targeting Christians, fundamentally disrupting the single-narrative thesis. The paper further examines how the conflation of ethnicity and religion in Nigerian public consciousness deepens societal fractures, and how external geopolitical framing introduces sovereign risk. It concludes with a policy agenda centred on constitutional accountability, security sector reform, climate adaptation, and the disruption of criminal economies. Nigeria's path to cohesion requires an inclusive security architecture that guarantees equal protection across all communities, not the elevation of one sector's suffering above another.

title: النموذج المعياري للتقرير الإداري النهائي في القرآن الكريم

detail.title: النموذج المعياري للتقرير الإداري النهائي في القرآن الكريم
detail.abstract: يهدف هذا البحث إلى استخراج نموذج معياري لكتابة التقرير الإداري الختامي من خلال قراءة تحليلية لسورة نوح في القرآن الكريم، استكمالاً لمشروع بحثي مستمرّ يُؤسِّس لاستنباط النماذج الإدارية من القصص القرآني. وقد اعتمد البحث المنهج الوصفي التحليلي المقارن، مع إفادة منضبطة من التفاسير السنية والشيعية، إضافةً إلى الأدبيات الإدارية المعاصرة في حقل الاتصال الإداري والتقارير الختامية للمشاريع. وتوصّل البحث إلى أن السورة الكريمة تنطوي على بنية تقرير إداري ختامي متكاملة، تتوزّع على أربعة مقاطع متتالية: الافتتاح بمخاطبة الجهة العليا، وعرض المهمة والمنهجية وردود الفعل، وإعلان النتيجة وتشخيص البنية المضادة، والتوصيات النهائية وأسبابها الموجبة. ويحكم هذه المقاطع ثمانية عشر ضابطاً معيارياً قابلاً للتطبيق على التقارير الإدارية المعاصرة. وقد جرى اختبار النموذج عبر «اختبار الاتساق العكسي» (Reverse Consistency Test) بإعادة كتابة تقرير نوح (عليه السلام) ذاته وفق النموذج المستخرَج. ويُكمل هذا البحث المنظومة المعيارية المزدوجة الواردة في كتاب «القيادة بين الإصلاح والثورة»، إذ يُمثّل نموذج نوح (عليه السلام) التقرير المُفصَّل للمهمة الممتدة، فيما يُمثّل نموذج يوسف (عليه السلام) التقرير الموجز للحدث المحدود، يحكمهما معاً معيار التناسب بين حجم التقرير وطبيعة موضوعه.

title: Only A Matter of Time? Evaluating Modeling Strategies While Building a National Operational Flood Forecast System for Denmark
affiliations: Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute, Danish Meteorological Institute, Danish Meteorological Institute, Danish Meteorological Institute, Danish Meteorological Institute, Danish Meteorological Institute, Danish Meteorological Institute, Danish Meteorological Institute, Danish Meteorological Institute, Danish Meteorological Institute, Danish Meteorological Institute, Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute, Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute and Danish Meteorological Institute

detail.title: Only A Matter of Time? Evaluating Modeling Strategies While Building a National Operational Flood Forecast System for Denmark
detail.abstract: In January 2022, the Danish Meteorological Institute was appointed the national flood warning authority for Denmark and tasked with developing an operational flood warning system within three years. Three different model development strategies were pursued in parallel to set up hydrological models for river discharge predictions, providing a unique real-world case study to compare their merits. A “top-down” model for Denmark was extracted from the process-based, pan-European E-HYPE model developed from large-scale data sources. A second process-based model, DK-HYPE, and a data-driven Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model were developed from the “bottom-up” using national data sources and high-resolution catchment delineations. This study evaluates the strategies not only in terms of classical model performance, but also by invested development time and operational benefits. Results show that the top-down approach enabled early operational readiness (1 day of work) and rapid development of operational workflows but was limited in its overall performance (KGE=0.50). The bottom-up process-based approach required significantly longer development efforts (19-32 months) but provided better model performance through local data and improved process representation (KGE=0.81). The data-driven approach gave the best model performance (KGE=0.91) with a relatively short development time (3-5 months). Despite lower overall performance, the top-down model proved competitive during two investigated flood events, highlighting its value in early system development. These findings demonstrate the benefits of a multi-model, hybrid development strategy, and provide practical guidance for the development of flood warning systems through a quantified case study.

title: A hundred ways to get flooded: systemic variation in disaster preparedness and response
affiliations: University of Reading, University of Reading, University of Reading and University of Reading

detail.title: A hundred ways to get flooded: systemic variation in disaster preparedness and response
detail.abstract: Flood early warning systems have improved in hazard detection, forecasting, and warning dissemination, yet a persistent gap between warning availability and protective action remains. This paper examines how flood warning information leads to action in municipal preparedness and early response, asking why municipalities act differently within the same system. Drawing on a nationwide cross-sectional survey of 46 municipalities in Luxembourg, a setting in which nationally standardised warnings are received directly without an intermediate administrative tier, we analyse how organisational arrangements condition whether interpretation of warning information results in action. Municipalities do not enter warning situations from equivalent starting points. Most lack formal intervention plans (69.6%) and predefined warning thresholds linking alert levels to specific measures (67.4%), creating uneven pre-warning institutional conditions. Warning information is not used as a direct trigger for action but assessed in relation to local conditions before measures are defined. This interpretive process is consistent across municipalities, with most reporting use of multiple information sources (97.8%) and local observation (76%). However, interpretation does not lead to action with the same frequency. Frequent action is observed exclusively in municipalities combining both a documented plan and a predefined threshold, while those without either element report the lowest action frequency. Institutional arrangements shape how often similar interpretive practices lead to action. The governance structure, in which municipalities retain responsibility for preparedness while operational emergency response is centralised, favours confirmation-based responses over anticipatory activation. Standardising warning signals does not standardise municipal response.
